title: Functions slot swaps, interrupted executions and bounded replay
banner: Training rehearsal - synthetic data - not a live Azure result
objective: Swap active Functions executions; distinguish termination/replay from guaranteed zero downtime.

sourceContract.readme: Functions, supported-plan slots: Test interrupted execution and replay; slot swaps alone do not guarantee zero downtime.
sourceContract.backlog: Add supporting-plan Functions slot swaps during active executions and replay.
sourceContract.acceptance: Native execution termination and bounded recovery are measured; duplicate effects are prevented; slot swaps alone cannot certify zero downtime.
sourceContract.portableCard: Swap active Functions executions; distinguish termination/replay from guaranteed zero downtime.
sourceContract.nativeSibling: Conduct one supported Functions swap; verify native execution outcomes and one intended business effect.

documentedConstraints.support: Consumption, Premium and eligible Dedicated plans support slots subject to plan limits. Flex Consumption has no deployment slots. Functions on Container Apps uses revisions.
documentedConstraints.routing: New trigger invocations route to the swapped slot during the routing switch.
documentedConstraints.termination: Slot swaps do not guarantee zero downtime; currently executing functions can be terminated and degraded availability can occur on scaled apps.
documentedConstraints.settings: Event-source and binding settings require deliberate slot-specific treatment before native swaps; this lesson changes no settings.
documentedConstraints.limits: The fixture is not evidence of any actual hosting plan, slot count, regional support, timeout, grace limit or native replay policy.

preconditions: All hosting, Functions, slots, triggers, executions, termination, replay, checkpoints, acknowledgments, effects, budgets and journeys are fixed fictional teaching DATA ONLY.
Two old-v1 executions are active before the fictional switch; one declared transition client starts on candidate-v2 after routing.
Queue effect invoice-42 is already committed at checkpoint 2 of 3 before acknowledgment loss.
The original queue journey times out at 14 ticks versus its 10-tick budget. The original HTTP execution and effects remain unknown.
A queue replay requires 6 fictional recovery ticks; only an exact typed integer 1 through 10 is allowed.
HTTP automatic retry and unknown-completion reconciliation are not provided or implied.
actions: Select a fixed hosting category, replay policy, recovery budget and explicit DATA ONLY confirmation.
Begin, record the swap, observe the probe, replay the queue work and check the independent measured results.
Compare deduplication, blind replay, insufficient recovery budget and unsupported hosting categories.
Inspect original executions, separate replay execution, checkpoints, acknowledgments, known effects and all started journeys.
Reset controls while retaining the complete bounded in-memory run history.
assertions: A successful swap or HTTP 200 never certifies execution continuity or adds compute.
Safe replay completes one recoverable queue item with one known effect; the original terminated execution and interruption stay recorded.
An unknown started HTTP execution stays in the 3-journey denominator after probe and queue replay.
Blind replay measures duplicate effects; a short recovery budget cannot manufacture completion, acknowledgment or checkpoint advancement.
Unsupported hosting has no exposure and no successful empty-sample claim.
Exact command fields, literal consent, numeric types, issued immutable states and phase guards reject coercion, forgery and repeated actions.
Reset preserves at most 6 runs and 6 ordered events per run without pruning.
Actual DOM, keyboard, visible errors/reset, missing model failure and CSP denials are observed.
